generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, integrating sources means using studies to support your argument, not reporting them one after another. The weaker habit lists what each study found, so the paragraph reads as a summary of the literature. The stronger habit puts your point first and brings studies in to back it, qualify it, or set up a contrast. The voices technique keeps your own voice in charge: you state the point, bring in supporting and contrasting studies, then close with your own judgement.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Consider two psychology students writing a paragraph that draws on the same four studies.

Tom writes: one study found an effect; another reported the same; a third noted a different pattern; a fourth found the effect had weakened. Each sentence reports a study, in the order he read them. The paragraph is accurate, but it has no point of its own. The reader learns what four authors found, not what Tom makes of it. This is reporting.

Amara opens in her own voice with the paragraph's point, then brings the studies in to serve it: a supporting study, a second that reinforces it, then a contrasting study that complicates the picture. She closes in her own voice with a short judgement that weighs them. The same four studies now support an argument. This is the voices technique.

Both students used the studies. Only Amara kept her own voice in charge of the paragraph.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, integrating sources means using studies to support your argument rather than reporting them. The voices technique keeps your own voice in charge: you state the point, bring in supporting and contrasting studies, then close with a judgement. You can now tell using a study from reporting it, and arrange several voices in a single paragraph. The next lesson sharpens this into a critical edge.

check.body: In the worked example, how did Amara weave the four studies into one paragraph?

items.text: Her own voice first, then supporting and contrasting studies, then a closing judgement.
By reporting each study in turn in the order she read them.
By removing the contrasting study so her point looked stronger.
By quoting all four studies at length with no comment.

feedback.correct: That's right. Amara led in her own voice and arranged supporting and contrasting studies around it.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for the option where Amara's voice frames the studies.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara opened in her own voice, brought in supporting and contrasting studies, and closed with a judgement. The others report, cut or quote.
